import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Dade's conjecture

Dade's conjecture relates the numbers of irreducible characters in the $p$-blocks of a finite
group $G$ to the numbers of irreducible characters in $p$-blocks of local subgroups, namely the
normalizers of chains of $p$-subgroups of $G$. This file states Dade's *ordinary conjecture*
(Dade 1992, Conjecture 6.3), the form referred to by the Wikipedia list entry.

We use the classical set-up of block theory (Isaacs, *Character theory of finite groups*, Ch. 15;
Navarro, *Characters and blocks of finite groups*, Ch. 3): fix a maximal ideal $M$ of the ring
$\mathbf{R}$ of algebraic integers in $\mathbb{C}$ with $p \in M$, so that $\mathbf{R}/M$ is an
algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$.

* For $\chi \in \operatorname{Irr}(G)$ the central character $\omega_\chi$ sends the class sum
  $K^+$ of a conjugacy class $K$ of $G$ to $\omega_\chi(K^+) = \sum_{x \in K} \chi(x)/\chi(1)
  = |K| \chi(g)/\chi(1) \in \mathbf{R}$ (for $g \in K$). Two irreducible characters of $G$ lie in
  the same $p$-block iff their central characters agree modulo $M$ on all class sums.
* For a subgroup $H \le G$, a $p$-block $b$ of $H$ and a $p$-block $B$ of $G$, the Brauer induced
  block $b^G$ is defined and equals $B$ iff
  $\omega_\chi(K^+) \equiv \omega_\psi((K \cap H)^+) \pmod M$ for all conjugacy classes $K$ of
  $G$, where $\psi \in b$, $\chi \in B$ and $(K \cap H)^+ = \sum_{h \in K \cap H} h$.
* The $p$-defect $d(\psi)$ of $\psi \in \operatorname{Irr}(H)$ is defined by
  $p^{d(\psi)} = |H|_p / \psi(1)_p$. The defect of a block is the maximum of the defects of its
  irreducible characters; in particular a block has positive defect iff it contains an
  irreducible character of positive defect.
* $O_p(H)$ denotes the largest normal $p$-subgroup of $H$.
* A *radical $p$-chain* of $G$ is a strictly increasing chain $C : P_0 < P_1 < \dots < P_n$ of
  $p$-subgroups of $G$ with $P_0 = O_p(G)$ and $P_i = O_p(N_G(P_0) \cap \dots \cap N_G(P_i))$ for
  all $i$. Its length is $|C| = n$ and its normalizer is
  $N_G(C) = N_G(P_0) \cap \dots \cap N_G(P_n)$. The group $G$ acts on the set $\mathcal{R}(G)$ of
  radical $p$-chains by conjugation.
* For $H \le G$, a block $B$ of $G$ and $d \ge 0$, $k(H, B, d)$ is the number of
  $\psi \in \operatorname{Irr}(H)$ with $d(\psi) = d$ whose block $b$ satisfies $b^G = B$.

**Dade's ordinary conjecture.** Let $G$ be a finite group and $p$ a prime with $O_p(G) = 1$. Then
for every $p$-block $B$ of $G$ of positive defect and every integer $d \ge 0$,
$$\sum_{C \in \mathcal{R}(G)/G} (-1)^{|C|} k(N_G(C), B, d) = 0,$$
where $C$ runs over a set of representatives of the $G$-conjugacy classes of radical $p$-chains.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Dade's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dade%27s_conjecture)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* E. C. Dade, *Counting characters in blocks. I*, Invent. Math. 109 (1992), 187–210.
  [doi:10.1007/BF01232023](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01232023)
* E. C. Dade, *Counting characters in blocks. II*, J. reine angew. Math. 448 (1994), 97–190.
  [doi:10.1515/crll.1994.448.97](https://doi.org/10.1515/crll.1994.448.97)
* E. C. Dade, *Counting characters in blocks. II.9*, in: Representation theory of finite groups
  (Columbus, OH, 1995), de Gruyter, Berlin, 1997, 45–59.
-/
namespace DadesConjecture
open scoped Pointwise
variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

blocks.code:
def pCore (p : ℕ) (H : Subgroup G) : Subgroup G :=
  sSup {P : Subgroup G | P ≤ H ∧ H ≤ P.normalizer ∧ IsPGroup p P}
blocks.docstring:
`O_p(H)` for a subgroup `H` of `G`, regarded as a subgroup of `G`: the largest normal
`p`-subgroup of `H`, i.e. the join of all `p`-subgroups `P ≤ H` that are normalized by `H`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Sylow, IsPGroup, Subgroup.normalCore, Subgroup.normalizer (none gives the p-core).
justification.name: DadesConjecture.pCore
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no O_p(G) (largest normal p-subgroup); needed for the chain definition and the hypothesis O_p(G)=1.

blocks.name: pCore

blocks.code:
def chainNormalizer (C : List (Subgroup G)) : Subgroup G :=
  ⨅ P ∈ C, P.normalizer
blocks.docstring:
The normalizer `N_G(C) = N_G(P₀) ∩ ⋯ ∩ N_G(Pₙ)` of a chain `C = [P₀, …, Pₙ]` of
subgroups.

justification.name: DadesConjecture.chainNormalizer
justification.why_needed: N_G(C) = ⋂ N_G(Pᵢ) for a list of subgroups; used both in the radical condition and for N_G(C).

blocks.name: chainNormalizer
blocks.text:
/-- The normalizer `N_G(C) = N_G(P₀) ∩ ⋯ ∩ N_G(Pₙ)` of a chain `C = [P₀, …, Pₙ]` of
subgroups. -/
def chainNormalizer (C : List (Subgroup G)) : Subgroup G :=
  ⨅ P ∈ C, P.normalizer

blocks.code:
structure RadicalPChain (p : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] where
  /-- The subgroups `P₀, …, Pₙ` of the chain, in increasing order. -/
  toList : List (Subgroup G)
  /-- The chain is nonempty. -/
  ne_nil : toList ≠ []
  /-- The chain is strictly increasing. -/
  sorted : toList.Pairwise (· < ·)
  /-- Every member of the chain is a `p`-subgroup. -/
  isPGroup : ∀ P ∈ toList, IsPGroup p P
  /-- `P₀ = O_p(G)`. -/
  head_eq : toList.head ne_nil = pCore p ⊤
  /-- `Pᵢ = O_p(N_G(Cᵢ))` where `Cᵢ : P₀ < ⋯ < Pᵢ` is the initial subchain. -/
  radical : ∀ i (hi : i < toList.length),
    toList[i] = pCore p (chainNormalizer (toList.take (i + 1)))
blocks.docstring:
A radical `p`-chain of `G` in the sense of Dade: a strictly increasing chain
`P₀ < P₁ < ⋯ < Pₙ` of `p`-subgroups of `G` such that `P₀ = O_p(G)` and
`Pᵢ = O_p(N_G(P₀) ∩ ⋯ ∩ N_G(Pᵢ))` for every `i`. The chain is recorded as the list
`[P₀, …, Pₙ]`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: List.Pairwise / List.Chain', Sylow's MulAut.conj pointwise action on subgroups, MulAction.orbitRel (would need a MulAction instance with nontrivial proofs).
justification.name: DadesConjecture.RadicalPChain (with length, normalizer, IsConj, IsConjClassRepresentatives, trivial)
justification.why_needed: Dade's radical p-chains, their length, normalizer, conjugation and sets of orbit representatives do not exist in Mathlib or the repo.

blocks.name: RadicalPChain
blocks.text:
/-- A radical `p`-chain of `G` in the sense of Dade: a strictly increasing chain
`P₀ < P₁ < ⋯ < Pₙ` of `p`-subgroups of `G` such that `P₀ = O_p(G)` and
`Pᵢ = O_p(N_G(P₀) ∩ ⋯ ∩ N_G(Pᵢ))` for every `i`. The chain is recorded as the list
`[P₀, …, Pₙ]`. -/
structure RadicalPChain (p : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] where
  /-- The subgroups `P₀, …, Pₙ` of the chain, in increasing order. -/
  toList : List (Subgroup G)
  /-- The chain is nonempty. -/
  ne_nil : toList ≠ []
  /-- The chain is strictly increasing. -/
  sorted : toList.Pairwise (· < ·)
  /-- Every member of the chain is a `p`-subgroup. -/
  isPGroup : ∀ P ∈ toList, IsPGroup p P
  /-- `P₀ = O_p(G)`. -/
  head_eq : toList.head ne_nil = pCore p ⊤
  /-- `Pᵢ = O_p(N_G(Cᵢ))` where `Cᵢ : P₀ < ⋯ < Pᵢ` is the initial subchain. -/
  radical : ∀ i (hi : i < toList.length),
    toList[i] = pCore p (chainNormalizer (toList.take (i + 1)))
namespace RadicalPChain
variable {p : ℕ}

blocks.code:
def IsConj (C C' : RadicalPChain p G) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : G, C'.toList = C.toList.map (MulAut.conj g • ·)
blocks.docstring:
Two radical `p`-chains are conjugate if some `g ∈ G` maps the first onto the second by
conjugation, `Pᵢ ↦ g Pᵢ g⁻¹`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: List.Pairwise / List.Chain', Sylow's MulAut.conj pointwise action on subgroups, MulAction.orbitRel (would need a MulAction instance with nontrivial proofs).
justification.name: DadesConjecture.RadicalPChain (with length, normalizer, IsConj, IsConjClassRepresentatives, trivial)
justification.why_needed: Dade's radical p-chains, their length, normalizer, conjugation and sets of orbit representatives do not exist in Mathlib or the repo.

blocks.name: IsConj
blocks.text:
/-- Two radical `p`-chains are conjugate if some `g ∈ G` maps the first onto the second by
conjugation, `Pᵢ ↦ g Pᵢ g⁻¹`. -/
def IsConj (C C' : RadicalPChain p G) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : G, C'.toList = C.toList.map (MulAut.conj g • ·)

blocks.code:
def IsConjClassRepresentatives (S : Finset (RadicalPChain p G)) : Prop :=
  ∀ C : RadicalPChain p G, ∃! C', C' ∈ S ∧ C.IsConj C'
blocks.docstring:
A finite set `S` of radical `p`-chains is a set of representatives of the `G`-conjugacy
classes of radical `p`-chains if every radical `p`-chain is conjugate to exactly one element of
`S`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: List.Pairwise / List.Chain', Sylow's MulAut.conj pointwise action on subgroups, MulAction.orbitRel (would need a MulAction instance with nontrivial proofs).
justification.name: DadesConjecture.RadicalPChain (with length, normalizer, IsConj, IsConjClassRepresentatives, trivial)
justification.why_needed: Dade's radical p-chains, their length, normalizer, conjugation and sets of orbit representatives do not exist in Mathlib or the repo.

blocks.name: IsConjClassRepresentatives
blocks.text:
/-- A finite set `S` of radical `p`-chains is a set of representatives of the `G`-conjugacy
classes of radical `p`-chains if every radical `p`-chain is conjugate to exactly one element of
`S`. -/
def IsConjClassRepresentatives (S : Finset (RadicalPChain p G)) : Prop :=
  ∀ C : RadicalPChain p G, ∃! C', C' ∈ S ∧ C.IsConj C'
end RadicalPChain

blocks.docstring:
`χ : G → ℂ` is the character of an irreducible complex representation of `G` of degree
`n`, that is, `χ(g)` is the trace of `ρ(g)` for an irreducible representation `ρ` of `G` on
`ℂⁿ`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: FDRep.character with CategoryTheory.Simple (forces G : Type 0), Representation.IsIrreducible, LinearMap.trace, padicValNat.
justification.name: DadesConjecture.IsIrrCharOfDegree / IsIrrCharOfDefect
justification.why_needed: Irreducible complex characters with their degree and p-defect; Mathlib has FDRep.character and Representation.IsIrreducible but no notion of 'irreducible character as a function' nor of p-defect.

blocks.name: IsIrrCharOfDegree
blocks.text:
/-- `χ : G → ℂ` is the character of an irreducible complex representation of `G` of degree
`n`, that is, `χ(g)` is the trace of `ρ(g)` for an irreducible representation `ρ` of `G` on
`ℂⁿ`. -/
def IsIrrCharOfDegree (n : ℕ) (χ : G → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ ρ : Representation ℂ G (Fin n → ℂ), ρ.IsIrreducible ∧
    ∀ g, χ g = LinearMap.trace ℂ (Fin n → ℂ) (ρ g)

blocks.code:
def IsIrrCharOfDefect (p d : ℕ) (χ : G → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ n, IsIrrCharOfDegree n χ ∧ padicValNat p (Nat.card G) = padicValNat p n + d
blocks.docstring:
`χ : G → ℂ` is an irreducible complex character of `G` of `p`-defect `d`, i.e.
$p^d = |G|_p / \chi(1)_p$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: FDRep.character with CategoryTheory.Simple (forces G : Type 0), Representation.IsIrreducible, LinearMap.trace, padicValNat.
justification.name: DadesConjecture.IsIrrCharOfDegree / IsIrrCharOfDefect
justification.why_needed: Irreducible complex characters with their degree and p-defect; Mathlib has FDRep.character and Representation.IsIrreducible but no notion of 'irreducible character as a function' nor of p-defect.

blocks.name: IsIrrCharOfDefect
blocks.text:
/-- `χ : G → ℂ` is an irreducible complex character of `G` of `p`-defect `d`, i.e.
$p^d = |G|_p / \chi(1)_p$. -/
def IsIrrCharOfDefect (p d : ℕ) (χ : G → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ n, IsIrrCharOfDegree n χ ∧ padicValNat p (Nat.card G) = padicValNat p n + d

blocks.code:
noncomputable def centralChar (χ : G → ℂ) (g : G) : ℂ :=
  ∑ᶠ x ∈ {x : G | IsConj g x}, χ x / χ 1
blocks.docstring:
The value $\omega_\chi(K^+) = \sum_{x \in K} \chi(x)/\chi(1)$ of the central character of
`χ` on the class sum of the conjugacy class `K` of `g` in `G`.

justification.name: DadesConjecture.centralChar / centralCharInter
justification.why_needed: Values ω_χ(K⁺) and ω_ψ((K∩H)⁺) of central characters on class sums, the ingredients of Brauer's definition of blocks and block induction; absent from Mathlib.

blocks.name: centralChar
blocks.text:
/-- The value $\omega_\chi(K^+) = \sum_{x \in K} \chi(x)/\chi(1)$ of the central character of
`χ` on the class sum of the conjugacy class `K` of `g` in `G`. -/
noncomputable def centralChar (χ : G → ℂ) (g : G) : ℂ :=
  ∑ᶠ x ∈ {x : G | IsConj g x}, χ x / χ 1

blocks.code:
noncomputable def centralCharInter (H : Subgroup G) (ψ : H → ℂ) (g : G) : ℂ :=
  ∑ᶠ h ∈ {h : H | IsConj g (h : G)}, ψ h / ψ 1
blocks.docstring:
For a character `ψ` of a subgroup `H ≤ G` and `g ∈ G` with `G`-conjugacy class `K`, the
value $\omega_\psi((K \cap H)^+) = \sum_{h \in K \cap H} \psi(h)/\psi(1)$ of the central character
of `ψ` on the sum of the elements of `H` that are conjugate in `G` to `g`.

justification.name: DadesConjecture.centralChar / centralCharInter
justification.why_needed: Values ω_χ(K⁺) and ω_ψ((K∩H)⁺) of central characters on class sums, the ingredients of Brauer's definition of blocks and block induction; absent from Mathlib.

blocks.name: centralCharInter
blocks.text:
/-- For a character `ψ` of a subgroup `H ≤ G` and `g ∈ G` with `G`-conjugacy class `K`, the
value $\omega_\psi((K \cap H)^+) = \sum_{h \in K \cap H} \psi(h)/\psi(1)$ of the central character
of `ψ` on the sum of the elements of `H` that are conjugate in `G` to `g`. -/
noncomputable def centralCharInter (H : Subgroup G) (ψ : H → ℂ) (g : G) : ℂ :=
  ∑ᶠ h ∈ {h : H | IsConj g (h : G)}, ψ h / ψ 1

blocks.docstring:
Brauer induction of blocks, with respect to the maximal ideal `M` of the algebraic integers:
the `p`-block `b` of `H ≤ G` containing the irreducible character `ψ` satisfies `b^G = B`, where
`B` is the `p`-block of `G` containing the irreducible character `χ`. This holds iff the central
characters satisfy $\omega_\chi(K^+) \equiv \omega_\psi((K \cap H)^+) \pmod M$ for every
conjugacy class `K` of `G`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: integralClosure ℤ ℂ, Ideal.IsMaximal (used as building blocks).
justification.name: DadesConjecture.BlockInducesTo
justification.why_needed: Brauer induction of blocks b^G = B (via central characters modulo a maximal ideal of the algebraic integers); Mathlib has no block theory.

blocks.name: BlockInducesTo
blocks.text:
/-- Brauer induction of blocks, with respect to the maximal ideal `M` of the algebraic integers:
the `p`-block `b` of `H ≤ G` containing the irreducible character `ψ` satisfies `b^G = B`, where
`B` is the `p`-block of `G` containing the irreducible character `χ`. This holds iff the central
characters satisfy $\omega_\chi(K^+) \equiv \omega_\psi((K \cap H)^+) \pmod M$ for every
conjugacy class `K` of `G`. -/
def BlockInducesTo (M : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ ℂ)) (H : Subgroup G) (ψ : H → ℂ)
    (χ : G → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, ∃ r ∈ M, (r : ℂ) = centralChar χ g - centralCharInter H ψ g

blocks.code:
noncomputable def numChars (p : ℕ) (M : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ ℂ)) (H : Subgroup G)
    (χ : G → ℂ) (d : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  {ψ : H → ℂ | IsIrrCharOfDefect p d ψ ∧ BlockInducesTo M H ψ χ}.ncard
blocks.docstring:
The number `k(H, B, d)` of irreducible characters `ψ` of the subgroup `H ≤ G` of `p`-defect
`d` whose `p`-block `b` satisfies `b^G = B`, where `B` is the `p`-block of `G` containing the
irreducible character `χ` of `G`.

justification.name: DadesConjecture.numChars
justification.why_needed: The count k(H, B, d) of irreducible characters of H of defect d in blocks inducing to B.

blocks.name: numChars
blocks.text:
/-- The number `k(H, B, d)` of irreducible characters `ψ` of the subgroup `H ≤ G` of `p`-defect
`d` whose `p`-block `b` satisfies `b^G = B`, where `B` is the `p`-block of `G` containing the
irreducible character `χ` of `G`. -/
noncomputable def numChars (p : ℕ) (M : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ ℂ)) (H : Subgroup G)
    (χ : G → ℂ) (d : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  {ψ : H → ℂ | IsIrrCharOfDefect p d ψ ∧ BlockInducesTo M H ψ χ}.ncard

blocks.code:
def RadicalPChain.trivial {p : ℕ} (h : pCore p (⊤ : Subgroup G) = ⊥) : RadicalPChain p G where
  toList := [⊥]
  ne_nil := by simp
  sorted := List.pairwise_singleton _ _
  isPGroup := by simpa using IsPGroup.of_bot
  head_eq := by simpa using h.symm
  radical i hi := by
    obtain rfl : i = 0 := by simpa using hi
    simpa [chainNormalizer, Subgroup.normalizer_eq_top] using h.symm
blocks.docstring: If `O_p(G) = 1`, the chain `1` of length `0` is a radical `p`-chain of `G`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: List.Pairwise / List.Chain', Sylow's MulAut.conj pointwise action on subgroups, MulAction.orbitRel (would need a MulAction instance with nontrivial proofs).

  toList := [⊥]

**Dade's ordinary conjecture** (Dade 1992, Conjecture 6.3). Let $G$ be a finite group and $p$ a
prime such that $O_p(G) = 1$. Let $B$ be a $p$-block of $G$ of positive defect and let $d \ge 0$.
Then
$$\sum_{C \in \mathcal{R}(G)/G} (-1)^{|C|} k(N_G(C), B, d) = 0,$$
where $C$ runs over a set of representatives of the $G$-conjugacy classes of radical $p$-chains
of $G$, $N_G(C)$ is the normalizer of $C$, and $k(N_G(C), B, d)$ is the number of irreducible
characters of $N_G(C)$ of $p$-defect $d$ lying in blocks $b$ of $N_G(C)$ with $b^G = B$.

Here blocks are taken with respect to a maximal ideal $M$ of the algebraic integers containing
$p$. The block $B$ is specified by an irreducible character $\chi \in B$; since the defect of a
block is the maximum of the defects of its characters, the blocks of positive defect are exactly

claims.decomposer_note: This is Dade's ordinary conjecture (Dade 1992, Conj. 6.3): for every finite group G and prime p with O_p(G) = 1, every p-block B of G of positive defect, and every d ≥ 0, the alternating sum Σ_C (-1)^{|C|} k(N_G(C), B, d) over G-orbit representatives of radical p-chains C (1 = P_0 < ... < P_n with P_i = O_p(∩_{j≤i} N_G(P_j))) is 0, where k(N_G(C), B, d) counts irreducible ordinary characters of N_G(C) of p-defect d lying in blocks b of N_G(C) with Brauer-induced block b^G = B; subtleties are the hypothesis O_p(G)=1 (needed, else the sum is trivially not over chains starting at 1), the positive-defect hypothesis (excludes defect-zero blocks where the sum is just k(B,0)≠0), the equivalence of radical/normal/elementary-abelian chain versions (Knörr–Robinson), and the fact that Mathlib has no blocks, defect, or Brauer correspondence, so these need bespoke definitions via central primitive idempotents of the group algebra over a p-modular system; the stronger projective/invariant/inductive refinements from Dade's later papers are not posed by the list entry and are omitted.
claims.reviewer_why: c01 states Dade's ordinary conjecture (Dade 1992, Conj. 6.3) most literally and with the safest bespoke definitions: blocks and Brauer induction via central characters modulo a maximal ideal M of the algebraic integers containing p (exactly Navarro Ch. 3-4 / Isaacs Ch. 15), radical p-chains as lists with P_0 = O_p(G) and P_i = O_p(∩_{j≤i} N_G(P_j)), sum over an arbitrary transversal of G-conjugacy classes with sign (-1)^n, k(N_G(C),B,d) counting irreducible character functions of N_G(C) of defect d (relative to N_G(C)) whose block induces to B, hypotheses O_p(G)=1 and d(B)>0 (encoded as d(χ)>0 for χ ∈ B, equivalent since defect-zero characters are alone in their block and d(B)=max d(χ)). Universe-polymorphic, irreducibility via Mathlib's Representation.IsIrreducible (nontrivial, no proper subreps). My only edit: the transversal S is a Finset and the sum is a Finset sum instead of a Set with finsum. c06/c07/c08 use the same textbook set-up and are also faithful, but c06 restricts G : Type, c07 chooses representatives via Quotient.out, and c08 replaces the orbit sum by a |N_G(C)|-weighted sum over all chains (equivalent but non-literal). c02/c03 quantify over arbitrary local domains O with algebraically closed fraction/residue fields; nothing forces O to contain the needed roots of unity, so for non-normal O the primitive central idempotents of O[H] need not be the p-blocks, putting the universally quantified statement at risk of falsity; they also model b^G = B by a defect-group/Brauer-map criterion (a theorem, not the definition). c04/c05 (DVR with ζ_|G| ∈ K) appear sound but are far heavier than the textbook formulation.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Dade's conjecture

Dade's conjecture relates the numbers of irreducible characters in the $p$-blocks of a finite
group $G$ to the numbers of irreducible characters in $p$-blocks of local subgroups, namely the
normalizers of chains of $p$-subgroups of $G$. This file states Dade's *ordinary conjecture*
(Dade 1992, Conjecture 6.3), the form referred to by the Wikipedia list entry.

We use the classical set-up of block theory (Isaacs, *Character theory of finite groups*, Ch. 15;
Navarro, *Characters and blocks of finite groups*, Ch. 3): fix a maximal ideal $M$ of the ring
$\mathbf{R}$ of algebraic integers in $\mathbb{C}$ with $p \in M$, so that $\mathbf{R}/M$ is an
algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$.

* For $\chi \in \operatorname{Irr}(G)$ the central character $\omega_\chi$ sends the class sum
  $K^+$ of a conjugacy class $K$ of $G$ to $\omega_\chi(K^+) = \sum_{x \in K} \chi(x)/\chi(1)
  = |K| \chi(g)/\chi(1) \in \mathbf{R}$ (for $g \in K$). Two irreducible characters of $G$ lie in
  the same $p$-block iff their central characters agree modulo $M$ on all class sums.
* For a subgroup $H \le G$, a $p$-block $b$ of $H$ and a $p$-block $B$ of $G$, the Brauer induced
  block $b^G$ is defined and equals $B$ iff
  $\omega_\chi(K^+) \equiv \omega_\psi((K \cap H)^+) \pmod M$ for all conjugacy classes $K$ of
  $G$, where $\psi \in b$, $\chi \in B$ and $(K \cap H)^+ = \sum_{h \in K \cap H} h$.
* The $p$-defect $d(\psi)$ of $\psi \in \operatorname{Irr}(H)$ is defined by
  $p^{d(\psi)} = |H|_p / \psi(1)_p$. The defect of a block is the maximum of the defects of its
  irreducible characters; in particular a block has positive defect iff it contains an
  irreducible character of positive defect.
* $O_p(H)$ denotes the largest normal $p$-subgroup of $H$.
* A *radical $p$-chain* of $G$ is a strictly increasing chain $C : P_0 < P_1 < \dots < P_n$ of
  $p$-subgroups of $G$ with $P_0 = O_p(G)$ and $P_i = O_p(N_G(P_0) \cap \dots \cap N_G(P_i))$ for
  all $i$. Its length is $|C| = n$ and its normalizer is
  $N_G(C) = N_G(P_0) \cap \dots \cap N_G(P_n)$. The group $G$ acts on the set $\mathcal{R}(G)$ of
  radical $p$-chains by conjugation.
* For $H \le G$, a block $B$ of $G$ and $d \ge 0$, $k(H, B, d)$ is the number of
  $\psi \in \operatorname{Irr}(H)$ with $d(\psi) = d$ whose block $b$ satisfies $b^G = B$.

**Dade's ordinary conjecture.** Let $G$ be a finite group and $p$ a prime with $O_p(G) = 1$. Then
for every $p$-block $B$ of $G$ of positive defect and every integer $d \ge 0$,
$$\sum_{C \in \mathcal{R}(G)/G} (-1)^{|C|} k(N_G(C), B, d) = 0,$$
where $C$ runs over a set of representatives of the $G$-conjugacy classes of radical $p$-chains.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Dade's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dade%27s_conjecture)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* E. C. Dade, *Counting characters in blocks. I*, Invent. Math. 109 (1992), 187–210.
  [doi:10.1007/BF01232023](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01232023)
* E. C. Dade, *Counting characters in blocks. II*, J. reine angew. Math. 448 (1994), 97–190.
  [doi:10.1515/crll.1994.448.97](https://doi.org/10.1515/crll.1994.448.97)
* E. C. Dade, *Counting characters in blocks. II.9*, in: Representation theory of finite groups
  (Columbus, OH, 1995), de Gruyter, Berlin, 1997, 45–59.
-/

namespace DadesConjecture

open scoped Pointwise

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- `O_p(H)` for a subgroup `H` of `G`, regarded as a subgroup of `G`: the largest normal
`p`-subgroup of `H`, i.e. the join of all `p`-subgroups `P ≤ H` that are normalized by `H`. -/
def pCore (p : ℕ) (H : Subgroup G) : Subgroup G :=
  sSup {P : Subgroup G | P ≤ H ∧ H ≤ P.normalizer ∧ IsPGroup p P}

/-- The normalizer `N_G(C) = N_G(P₀) ∩ ⋯ ∩ N_G(Pₙ)` of a chain `C = [P₀, …, Pₙ]` of
subgroups. -/
def chainNormalizer (C : List (Subgroup G)) : Subgroup G :=
  ⨅ P ∈ C, P.normalizer

/-- A radical `p`-chain of `G` in the sense of Dade: a strictly increasing chain
`P₀ < P₁ < ⋯ < Pₙ` of `p`-subgroups of `G` such that `P₀ = O_p(G)` and
`Pᵢ = O_p(N_G(P₀) ∩ ⋯ ∩ N_G(Pᵢ))` for every `i`. The chain is recorded as the list
`[P₀, …, Pₙ]`. -/
structure RadicalPChain (p : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] where
  /-- The subgroups `P₀, …, Pₙ` of the chain, in increasing order. -/
  toList : List (Subgroup G)
  /-- The chain is nonempty. -/
  ne_nil : toList ≠ []
  /-- The chain is strictly increasing. -/
  sorted : toList.Pairwise (· < ·)
  /-- Every member of the chain is a `p`-subgroup. -/
  isPGroup : ∀ P ∈ toList, IsPGroup p P
  /-- `P₀ = O_p(G)`. -/
  head_eq : toList.head ne_nil = pCore p ⊤
  /-- `Pᵢ = O_p(N_G(Cᵢ))` where `Cᵢ : P₀ < ⋯ < Pᵢ` is the initial subchain. -/
  radical : ∀ i (hi : i < toList.length),
    toList[i] = pCore p (chainNormalizer (toList.take (i + 1)))

namespace RadicalPChain

variable {p : ℕ}

/-- The length `|C| = n` of the radical `p`-chain `C : P₀ < ⋯ < Pₙ`. -/
def length (C : RadicalPChain p G) : ℕ := C.toList.length - 1

/-- The normalizer `N_G(C) = N_G(P₀) ∩ ⋯ ∩ N_G(Pₙ)` of the radical `p`-chain `C`. -/
def normalizer (C : RadicalPChain p G) : Subgroup G := chainNormalizer C.toList

/-- Two radical `p`-chains are conjugate if some `g ∈ G` maps the first onto the second by
conjugation, `Pᵢ ↦ g Pᵢ g⁻¹`. -/
def IsConj (C C' : RadicalPChain p G) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : G, C'.toList = C.toList.map (MulAut.conj g • ·)

/-- A finite set `S` of radical `p`-chains is a set of representatives of the `G`-conjugacy
classes of radical `p`-chains if every radical `p`-chain is conjugate to exactly one element of
`S`. -/
def IsConjClassRepresentatives (S : Finset (RadicalPChain p G)) : Prop :=
  ∀ C : RadicalPChain p G, ∃! C', C' ∈ S ∧ C.IsConj C'

end RadicalPChain

/-- `χ : G → ℂ` is the character of an irreducible complex representation of `G` of degree
`n`, that is, `χ(g)` is the trace of `ρ(g)` for an irreducible representation `ρ` of `G` on
`ℂⁿ`. -/
def IsIrrCharOfDegree (n : ℕ) (χ : G → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ ρ : Representation ℂ G (Fin n → ℂ), ρ.IsIrreducible ∧
    ∀ g, χ g = LinearMap.trace ℂ (Fin n → ℂ) (ρ g)

/-- `χ : G → ℂ` is an irreducible complex character of `G` of `p`-defect `d`, i.e.
$p^d = |G|_p / \chi(1)_p$. -/
def IsIrrCharOfDefect (p d : ℕ) (χ : G → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ n, IsIrrCharOfDegree n χ ∧ padicValNat p (Nat.card G) = padicValNat p n + d

/-- The value $\omega_\chi(K^+) = \sum_{x \in K} \chi(x)/\chi(1)$ of the central character of
`χ` on the class sum of the conjugacy class `K` of `g` in `G`. -/
noncomputable def centralChar (χ : G → ℂ) (g : G) : ℂ :=
  ∑ᶠ x ∈ {x : G | IsConj g x}, χ x / χ 1

/-- For a character `ψ` of a subgroup `H ≤ G` and `g ∈ G` with `G`-conjugacy class `K`, the
value $\omega_\psi((K \cap H)^+) = \sum_{h \in K \cap H} \psi(h)/\psi(1)$ of the central character
of `ψ` on the sum of the elements of `H` that are conjugate in `G` to `g`. -/
noncomputable def centralCharInter (H : Subgroup G) (ψ : H → ℂ) (g : G) : ℂ :=
  ∑ᶠ h ∈ {h : H | IsConj g (h : G)}, ψ h / ψ 1

/-- Brauer induction of blocks, with respect to the maximal ideal `M` of the algebraic integers:
the `p`-block `b` of `H ≤ G` containing the irreducible character `ψ` satisfies `b^G = B`, where
`B` is the `p`-block of `G` containing the irreducible character `χ`. This holds iff the central
characters satisfy $\omega_\chi(K^+) \equiv \omega_\psi((K \cap H)^+) \pmod M$ for every
conjugacy class `K` of `G`. -/
def BlockInducesTo (M : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ ℂ)) (H : Subgroup G) (ψ : H → ℂ)
    (χ : G → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, ∃ r ∈ M, (r : ℂ) = centralChar χ g - centralCharInter H ψ g

/-- The number `k(H, B, d)` of irreducible characters `ψ` of the subgroup `H ≤ G` of `p`-defect
`d` whose `p`-block `b` satisfies `b^G = B`, where `B` is the `p`-block of `G` containing the
irreducible character `χ` of `G`. -/
noncomputable def numChars (p : ℕ) (M : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ ℂ)) (H : Subgroup G)
    (χ : G → ℂ) (d : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  {ψ : H → ℂ | IsIrrCharOfDefect p d ψ ∧ BlockInducesTo M H ψ χ}.ncard

/-- `O_p(H)` is contained in `H`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem pCore_le (p : ℕ) (H : Subgroup G) : pCore p H ≤ H :=
  sSup_le fun _ hP => hP.1

/-- Every radical `p`-chain is conjugate to itself. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem RadicalPChain.isConj_self {p : ℕ} (C : RadicalPChain p G) : C.IsConj C :=
  ⟨1, by simp⟩

/-- If `O_p(G) = 1`, the chain `1` of length `0` is a radical `p`-chain of `G`. -/
def RadicalPChain.trivial {p : ℕ} (h : pCore p (⊤ : Subgroup G) = ⊥) : RadicalPChain p G where
  toList := [⊥]
  ne_nil := by simp
  sorted := List.pairwise_singleton _ _
  isPGroup := by simpa using IsPGroup.of_bot
  head_eq := by simpa using h.symm
  radical i hi := by
    obtain rfl : i = 0 := by simpa using hi
    simpa [chainNormalizer, Subgroup.normalizer_eq_top] using h.symm

/-- The chain `1` has length `0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem RadicalPChain.length_trivial {p : ℕ} (h : pCore p (⊤ : Subgroup G) = ⊥) :
    (RadicalPChain.trivial h).length = 0 := rfl

/-- The normalizer of the chain `1` is `G`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem RadicalPChain.normalizer_trivial {p : ℕ} (h : pCore p (⊤ : Subgroup G) = ⊥) :
    (RadicalPChain.trivial h).normalizer = ⊤ := by
  simp [RadicalPChain.trivial, RadicalPChain.normalizer, chainNormalizer,
    Subgroup.normalizer_eq_top]

/-- An irreducible character of degree `n` takes the value `n` at the identity. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsIrrCharOfDegree.apply_one {n : ℕ} {χ : G → ℂ} (h : IsIrrCharOfDegree n χ) :
    χ 1 = n := by
  obtain ⟨ρ, -, hχ⟩ := h
  simp [hχ]

/-- The central character takes the value `1` on the class sum of the identity. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem centralChar_one {χ : G → ℂ} (hχ : χ 1 ≠ 0) : centralChar χ 1 = 1 := by
  simp [centralChar, hχ]

/--
**Dade's ordinary conjecture** (Dade 1992, Conjecture 6.3). Let $G$ be a finite group and $p$ a
prime such that $O_p(G) = 1$. Let $B$ be a $p$-block of $G$ of positive defect and let $d \ge 0$.
Then
$$\sum_{C \in \mathcal{R}(G)/G} (-1)^{|C|} k(N_G(C), B, d) = 0,$$
where $C$ runs over a set of representatives of the $G$-conjugacy classes of radical $p$-chains
of $G$, $N_G(C)$ is the normalizer of $C$, and $k(N_G(C), B, d)$ is the number of irreducible
characters of $N_G(C)$ of $p$-defect $d$ lying in blocks $b$ of $N_G(C)$ with $b^G = B$.

Here blocks are taken with respect to a maximal ideal $M$ of the algebraic integers containing
$p$. The block $B$ is specified by an irreducible character $\chi \in B$; since the defect of a
block is the maximum of the defects of its characters, the blocks of positive defect are exactly
the blocks of the irreducible characters $\chi$ of positive defect.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem dades_conjecture {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime)
    (hG : pCore p (⊤ : Subgroup G) = ⊥)
    (M : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ ℂ)) [M.IsMaximal] (hpM : (p : integralClosure ℤ ℂ) ∈ M)
    {χ : G → ℂ} {e : ℕ} (hχ : IsIrrCharOfDefect p e χ) (he : 0 < e) (d : ℕ)
    {S : Finset (RadicalPChain p G)} (hS : RadicalPChain.IsConjClassRepresentatives S) :
    ∑ C ∈ S, (-1 : ℤ) ^ C.length * numChars p M C.normalizer χ d = 0 := by
  sorry

end DadesConjecture

items: The Wikipedia list entry is a one-line description; following the decomposition table it is formalized as Dade's ordinary conjecture (Dade 1992, Conjecture 6.3), with radical p-chains (Dade's own chain family), hypothesis O_p(G)=1, blocks of positive defect, and all d ≥ 0. The projective/invariant/inductive refinements are not stated.

p-modular system: blocks are defined via the classical Isaacs/Navarro set-up — a maximal ideal M of the ring integralClosure ℤ ℂ of algebraic integers with p ∈ M (so R/M is an algebraically closed field of characteristic p). The theorem is universally quantified over such M. Dade's conjecture is asserted for an arbitrary (large enough) p-modular system, so quantifying over all M is faithful; it is also standard that the block partition does not depend on M.

Brauer induction b^G = B is encoded by BlockInducesTo: for all g ∈ G, ω_χ(K_g^+) − ω_ψ((K_g ∩ H)^+) ∈ M, i.e. λ_B(K^+) = λ_b((K∩H)^+) on every class sum; this is the standard definition of b^G (b^G is defined iff λ_b^G is an algebra homomorphism, i.e. equals some λ_B). When b^G is undefined no B satisfies the condition, matching the convention that such characters are not counted. For chain normalizers b^G is in fact always defined (transitivity along the chain).

A block B is specified by an irreducible character χ ∈ B; 'B has positive defect' is rendered as 'χ has positive p-defect'. Since the defect of a block is the maximum of the defects of its characters (every block contains a height-zero character; Isaacs even takes this as the definition of d(B)), the blocks of positive defect are exactly the blocks B(χ) with d(χ) > 0, and the sum depends only on B(χ).

Irreducible characters are represented as functions χ : G → ℂ given by traces of an irreducible representation (Representation.IsIrreducible) on Fin n → ℂ; every irreducible complex character arises this way, and n = χ(1) gives the degree. The p-defect is encoded as padicValNat p |H| = padicValNat p n + d (no truncated subtraction). Counting characters via Set.ncard on functions identifies isomorphic representations, as required for k(H,B,d).
O_p(H) (for H ≤ G, as a subgroup of G) is defined as the sSup of all p-subgroups P ≤ H normalized by H; for finite groups this is the largest normal p-subgroup.

Radical p-chains are lists [P₀,…,Pₙ] of p-subgroups, strictly increasing, with P₀ = O_p(G) and Pᵢ = O_p(N_G(P₀) ∩ ⋯ ∩ N_G(Pᵢ)) for every i (Dade's definition; for i = 0 the condition is automatic). Length |C| = n and N_G(C) = ⋂ N_G(Pᵢ), which is the stabilizer of C under conjugation.

The sum over R(G)/G is formalized as a sum over an arbitrary set S of representatives of the conjugacy classes of radical p-chains (∀ S, IsConjClassRepresentatives S → Σ_{C∈S} … = 0), with conjugation given by the pointwise MulAut.conj action on subgroups. The sum uses finsum (∑ᶠ C ∈ S); S is finite because a finite group has finitely many strictly increasing chains of subgroups, so finsum agrees with the actual sum.
Primality is a hypothesis (hp : p.Prime) rather than a Fact instance, since no instance needs it; the theorem is universe-polymorphic in G.

reviewer_notes: The Wikipedia list entry is a one-line description; per the decomposition table it is formalized as Dade's ordinary conjecture over radical p-chains (Dade 1992, Conj. 6.3); the projective/invariant/inductive refinements are not stated. All eight candidates compiled and all interpreted the slot the same way; none omitted it. Modeling choices shipped: (1) blocks are defined with respect to an arbitrary maximal ideal M of integralClosure ℤ ℂ with p ∈ M (theorem quantifies over all such M; the block partition is known to be independent of M, and Dade asserts the conjecture for any such choice); (2) 'b^G = B' is encoded as λ_b^G = λ_B on all class sums, i.e. Σ_{h∈N∩Cl_G(g)} ψ(h)/ψ(1) ≡ |Cl_G(g)|χ(g)/χ(1) mod M for all g ∈ G — this is Navarro's definition, and when λ_b^G is not a block character no B satisfies it, matching the convention that such characters are not counted (for chain normalizers b^G is always defined anyway); (3) the block B is given by an irreducible character χ ∈ B with d(χ) > 0, equivalent to d(B) > 0; (4) the sum is over any finite set S of orbit representatives (∀ S with the transversal property), which exists since a finite group has finitely many radical chains, so the statement is non-vacuous; (5) if p ∤ |G| there are no positive-defect blocks and the statement is vacuous, consistent with the source. Boundary check: the trivial chain [1] is a radical p-chain when O_p(G)=1 (tested in the file), with normalizer G and length 0, so k(G,B,d) enters with sign +1 as in Dade. Compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning.
